summary: Canary affinity loss after hotfix cutover causing unexpected fallback to baseline model
description: Issue summary: After a hotfix cutover in routing (rolled 2026-03-11 03:30 UTC), certain customers using model-version pins combined with a low-weight canary observed a sudden loss of canary affinity. Impact: ~8-12% of requests that should have remained pinned to the canary variant were routed to the baseline model, leading to higher token costs and functional regressions for pinned traffic. Environment: prod-us-east-1, Dedicated pool for Clipscribe (customer tenant ID: clip-98). Impact window started ~2026-03-11T03:35Z and persisted until a manual mitigation at ~2026-03-11T08:10Z for the affected tenant. Expected: Pinning a session or API key to a specific model variant must prevent fallback to baseline unless explicit fallback policy triggers. Actual: Many pinned sessions lost affinity transiently and hit the baseline variant despite pin metadata. Steps to reproduce: 1) Tenant with dedicated routing and model pin to gptj-6b-v2; 2) Canary rollout active with 10% weight for gptj-6b-quant and baseline at 90%; 3) Deploy hotfix that modifies routing hash normalization (routing v2 hotfix); 4) Replay 2k requests with identical session_id and prompt; 5) Observe 80-90 requests routed to baseline unexpectedly (logs attached). Example logs: request_id=rb-20260311-7a4, route_hash=0x3b4a, selected_model=gptj-6b, pin_header=x-model-pin=gptj-6b-v2 -> routed to baseline. Impact notes: customer reports degraded output quality for pinned sessions and billing spike. This is customer-visible and time-sensitive.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure canary (gptj-6b-quant) is at 10% weight and model pin header x-model-pin is set to gptj-6b-v2. 2) From a pinned API key, send 2k short context requests using the same session_id over 5 minutes. 3) Check routing decisions in routing logs /dashboards for session_id. 4) Observe ~4-6% of requests routed to baseline instead of pinned variant during hotfix cutover.

2026-03-11 04:20 - Derek O'Neil: Triage, escalating to SRE & routing owners. Assigning to canary-controller and routing owners. Collecting routing logs and binary hashes.

2026-03-11 05:10 - Lina Chen (SRE): Found a change in routing hash normalization in commit 9f3a2b4f that strips leading zeros from session hash; hypothesizing sticky-affinity key mismatch against stored canary affinity table.

2026-03-11 07:45 - Derek O'Neil: Applied tenant-specific override to force route selection using explicit x-model-pin header for Clipscribe. Early telemetry shows pinned ratio restored to ~99.8%.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Derek O'Neil: Filed internal postmortem task and scheduled patch; customer notified of workaround. Pending full deploy of fix in routing v2 to restore normalization compatibility.

2026-03-13 10:15 - Lina Chen: Root-cause patch merged to main (PR #4521) to reintroduce normalization shim and add a compatibility flag. Patch scheduled for deploy in the next safe window (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: hotfix changed session-hash normalization which caused previously computed canary-affinity table keys (persisted) to no longer match incoming request keys, triggering routing fallback. Evidence: matched timestamped request IDs where stored affinity key was '0x00ab4' but incoming normalized key was '0xab4' after hotfix. Checks performed: - Cross-referenced routing logs (s3://logs/routing/prod/2026-03-11) - Verified commit 9f3a2b4f touched routing/normalize.py - Replayed requests in staging with and without normalization change reproduces drift. Metrics: canary-hit-rate for pinned sessions dropped from 99.9% to 91.2% during cutover. Related code paths: canary-controller sticky_map lookup, serving-router selection fallback path, prefix normalization util. Temporary mitigation: tenant override to respect explicit x-model-pin header before affinity table lookup. Work required: restore backward-compatible normalization; add migration step to rebuild affinity table keys; add e2e test for pin + canary hotfix deployments.
resolution_notes: Short-term (applied 2026-03-11 07:45 UTC): tenant-scoped routing override for Clipscribe forcing header-respected selection. This restored pinned behavior for the customer.
resolution: Long-term fix: PR #4521 merged to reintroduce compatibility shim and add a feature flag 'normalize_compat_mode' defaulted ON for 2 weeks; scheduled deploy 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Migration: a background job to rebuild canary-affinity keys for active tenants will run post-deploy to eliminate lingering mismatches. Customer notified and monitoring set up. Follow-ups: add automated canary-affinity regression test to CI, add runbook step for hotfixes that change hashing/normalization. Patch rollout plan attached in Confluence.
